items.title: Fourier-space density decay implies decay of physical-space Sobolev norms
items.author: Marnie Smith
items.work: Uniform semiclassical nonlinear Hartree phase mixing and weighted scattering for small perturbations
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the unlabelled corollary at source lines 376-391, headed [Physical-space decay]: under the hypotheses of the main theorem, for every n below $\sigma_1$1 minus d times one minus one over p, the weighted Lp norm of the density is bounded by a constant times a negative power of time. The author gave it no label, so its position in the article is part of its identity. The proof (source lines 392-399) is short but not formal: the Hausdorff-Young inequality has to be applied to the weighted norm rather than to the plain one, which is what produces the dual exponent p' inside the frequency integral, and the convergence of that integral, after the decay estimate is substituted, is exactly where the restriction on n comes from. Both the dual exponent bookkeeping and the convergence condition are absent from the statement.
